q: 1. Mechanical weathering of soils is caused by .............
explain: Mechanical (physical) weathering results from temperature cycling, water action, and ice wedging combined.

q: 2. A civil engineer is mainly concerned with .......... top mantle of soil in dealing with small and medium sized projects.
explain: For typical small-to-medium projects, engineering interest and exploration generally extends to about 10-15 m depth.

q: 3. Honey combed structure is found in .............
explain: Honeycomb structure, formed by arching of bulky grains bridging over pore spaces, is characteristic of coarse sands (and fine sands/silts under certain deposition).

q: 4. Soil transported by water and deposited at the bottom of the lake is known as .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'loess'; by standard definition, soil deposited at the bottom of a lake is actually called lacustrine soil, and loess is wind-deposited.

q: 5. Who coined the term soil mechanics?
explain: Karl Terzaghi, considered the father of soil mechanics, coined the term and founded the discipline.
Loess is a fine-grained, wind-deposited (aeolian) soil formed from accumulated silt-sized particles.
Peat is a highly organic soil formed from decomposed and partially decayed vegetable/plant matter.

q: 8. When the particles of soil are oriented 'edge to edge' or 'edge to face' with respect to one another, the soil is said to have .............
explain: Edge-to-edge or edge-to-face particle orientation, common in clay deposition, produces a loose, open flocculent structure.
Per the reference key, peat is classified here as organic clay, reflecting its high organic decomposed plant matter content.
Under-reamed piles are a type of bored (cast-in-situ) pile with an enlarged base, formed by drilling rather than driving.
